subject.title: Feature: --agent flag for TUI to select which agent handles the session

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support `openclaw tui --agent <id>` as a public startup selector, and what precedence should it have over agent-scoped `--session` values and workspace inference?
rationale: The missing capability is established, but a public CLI flag changes durable agent, model, workspace, and session-routing semantics; source inspection cannot choose the intended precedence contract.

options.title: Add an explicit selector
options.body: Add a validated `--agent <id>` and document a clear precedence order while preserving current behavior when it is omitted.

options.title: Keep current routing mechanisms
options.body: Retain workspace inference and canonical agent-scoped session keys without adding another public TUI selector.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit selector
recommendation.body: Add a validated `--agent <id>` and document a clear precedence order while preserving current behavior when it is omitted.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue already has a recent routing assessment from steipete, and the remaining choice is a durable TUI CLI contract rather than only the earlier workspace implementation.
